title: Python: a re-export hop reads the hop module's bindings after del or reassignment, and a comprehension target does not bind in the same-module path (DEC-303 (a49) item 5)
description: DEC-303 (a49) item 5, opum-ai/opum-doc#2016 (ODOC-640), 2026-11-26T11:43Z, verbatim: 'N3, a re-export hop that resolves n.f without reading n's bindings after del f or f = wrap(f), predates #183. It is the wrong-edge class: GCLI-116's own invariant, one hop further. It gets its own task, together with N1's same-module path, and lands before the freeze. It may share code with NB-b, in the leader's order.' Found by the #183 round 1 review. Parts: (0) N2 (added by DEC-303 (a50) item 3-4): see the N2 paragraph below. (1) N3: symbolInModuleOrReexport and the module-attribute re-export chain follow from n import f hops without reading n's module-level bindings of f, so n.py: from m import f / del f (or f = wrap(f)) still resolves from n import f; f() to m.f; the gate in resolveImportBinding and resolveModuleAttribute reads the bindings of the directly named module only. (2) N1 same-module path: a comprehension iteration target is recorded by the walker as a binding of the enclosing scope (comprehension: true) and the same-module bare-name path counts it, so a module-level def f plus _ = [0 for f in X] makes f rebound for a same-module call although Python binds the target in the comprehension's own scope (a walrus target inside a comprehension still binds the enclosing scope, PEP 572). Build: red/green fixtures with callee-symbol pinning and the full bin delta, positive twins, mutation checks by name, and the five-pin corpus diff per (a34) and (a40) item 2 with every in-repo edge created or removed reported before the clear. Lands before the analyzer freezes for the blind sample; joins the (a36) item 1(i) hold list (a49 item 7). Not built until the leader sends the GO. N2 (DEC-303 (a50) items 3 and 4, opum-ai/opum-doc#2017, 2026-11-26T11:51Z, folded into this task, no separate N2 task): N2 is still a defect against a rule in force. The gate (moduleBindingGate) ignores a star import in m; it must apply (a12) N3 walk to a star import in m, as enumerableBindings already does for the bare name: walk the star imports from last to first; a complete one that exports the name decides it; a complete one that does not export it is skipped; a partial one reached first leaves the name star-bound and unresolved. Count on the five pins (glyph-cli, #183 head f2a6b2e, 2026-11-26): resolved cross-file edges whose callee is a module-level def of a module m with a module-level star import: flask 0 of 538, jinja 0 of 775, httpx 0 of 1042, rich 0 of 2982, tqdm 0 of 293; nothing is expected to move on the pins. Caveat: the count keys on callees defined in m and is a conservative superset in the sense that it also counts any star that cannot bind the name; a name m only re-exports through a star is not counted. Lands before the freeze with this task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: n.py re-exporting f from m then del f or f = wrap(f): from n import f; f() and import n; n.f() resolve to no edge and are binned as a rebound name is; the twin without the del resolves to m.f, callee pinned, full bin delta

a same-module call to a def f with a comprehension target named f at module level resolves (the target is not a module binding); a walrus target inside a comprehension still makes f rebound; function-level behaviour unchanged
five-pin corpus diff script-asserted, each moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear
mutation checks by name, each red

N2: a star import in m is walked last to first per (a12) N3: a def f in m followed by from x import * where x complete and exports f makes the cross-module call resolve as the star-bound name (not m.f); where x is complete and does not export f, the def stands; where x is partial (unresolved, external, non-literal __all__) and reached first, the name is star-bound and unresolved; red/green fixtures for from-import and module-attribute calls with callee pinning and the full bin delta, each with a twin, mutation checks by name

plan: N3: moduleBindingGate reads a re-exporting module once it has a second binding of the name, and sourceChainOutcome walks the from-import's source module and each lone-import hop after it, following aliases (name = hop.name ?? hop.boundName), in resolveImportBinding and resolveModuleAttribute. N1: comprehension targets record their range and are dropped from a module name's bindings for a read outside it (resolveBareName). N2: starOverride orders a holder's module-level stars against the name's bindings last to first. Retire A2's interim single-binding refusal.
implementationNotes: DEC-303 (a50) items 3 and 4 (N2 folded into this task; the earlier filing in #186 did not carry it): see the N2 paragraph appended to the description and the added acceptance criterion. Count 0 on the five pins; lands before the freeze.

DEC-303 (a52) item 1 and (a53), GCLI-117 (opum-ai/glyph-cli#190): A2's moduleClassMemberCall refuses, as an interim local to that path, unless the holder module has exactly ONE module-scope binding of the class name (comment names GCLI-118 as its retirement). When this task lands the general hop reading and A2 reads through that gate, a complete star that exports the name resolves, and the two httpx edges tests/test_status_codes.py:23:12 and tests/test_status_codes.py:27:12 (httpx.codes.get_reason_phrase, httpx/__init__.py binds codes only through from ._status_codes import *, __all__ = [codes]) are EXPECTED BACK in this task's corpus diff; the A2 refusal then retires.

DEC-303 (a54) item 3: the second-hop rebind shape is a GCLI-118 fixture. m.py has from n import C, and n.py has from o import C plus C = None; m.C.meth() (and the bare from-import form) still gets the first-pick edge to o.C.meth at GCLI-117's head, because resolveModuleAttribute reads only the first import binding at each hop and A2's single-binding refusal counts only m's own module scope. The general hop reading must refuse it, with a refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the site and the bin is unchanged.

Landed 2026-11-26 in opum-ai/glyph-cli#198 as squash b3fd5d3e (final head 05d81e92, two Opus rounds, a capped confirmatory check, rulings DEC-303 (a59) to (a63)). Pin corpus (flask 49943b5a, httpx 7cff5f79, jinja 5ef70112, rich 3a109ccd, tqdm 9cf5a12b) vs origin/dev 3179ed27: exactly two in-repo edges created, tests/test_status_codes.py:23:12 and :27:12 to httpx/_status_codes.py:39:9 (codes.get_reason_phrase), plain, expected back per (a53) and accepted in (a59); none removed; the differences on no-pin shapes (star ordering against defs, imports and conditional bindings) were named to opum-doc and accepted in (a59), (a60), (a62), (a63). The corpus diff was a throwaway script run on a git archive of dev and on each head; it is not committed.

Known limits (DEC-303 (a62) items 5 and 6, (a63)): an import in a finally, or in a try body with only a finally, stays an alternative through S3's own condition; N-2's order-blind case (from o import f; from x import * then def f gives [m.f, o.f] multi where Python gives m.f); a case-arm def is an alternative while a case-arm assignment still refuses (defs and classes use maySkipStatement, assignments keep isConditionalStatement); an unpositioned rebinding before a star gives no edge (lost, not wrong); N1 applies in resolveBareName only (isUnshadowedBuiltin and resolveStarAttribute's holder check still see the comprehension target); a conditional hop ends the chain walk (a refusal not extended); the one-line star shape (from o import f; from x import * on one line) is the (a60) item 3 tie, unresolved. Follow-ups: GCLI-124 (item 9), GCLI-125 (N-6), GCLI-126 (imports given the may-skip walk).
finalSummary: A re-export hop now reads the hop modules' own bindings (del, reassignment, second import, aliases followed), a module-level comprehension target binds nothing outside its comprehension, a holder's star imports are ordered against the name's bindings (last to first, ties and unpositioned bindings unresolved, conditional defs, classes and imports after a star as alternatives), and A2's interim single-binding refusal is retired. Verified by 39 fixtures in test/python-hops.test.ts (both forms, callee pinned, full bin delta, each red on the earlier head and green after), mutants observed red per rule, 1025 tests and four CI checks green on the landed head, and the five-pin diff: only the two expected httpx edges created, none removed.
